name: The Constitution of Humanity (Body and Soul)

objectives.text: Identify that God made each person with a body and a soul
Retell how God formed Adam's body from the dust and breathed into him the breath of life
Explain that the human body God made is good and not something bad or shameful
Describe from a Gospel account how Jesus cared for both a person's body and soul
Describe what Scripture teaches happens to the body and to the soul when a person dies
Summarize the Reformed teaching that a human being is one person made of a material body and an immaterial soul
Explain from the Gospels that Jesus took to himself a true human body and a reasonable soul
Compare the intermediate state, in which the believer's soul is with Christ, with the final resurrection of the body
Explain the Heidelberg Catechism's teaching that a believer belongs to Christ in body and soul, in life and in death
Apply Paul's call to glorify God in the body to everyday choices about work, rest, food, and care of the body
Analyze the dichotomist and trichotomist views of human nature using the biblical evidence each side cites
Interpret 1 Thessalonians 5:23 and Hebrews 4:12 in their literary context to determine whether they divide the person into separate parts
Explain why the Christian hope centers on the resurrection of the body and not on the soul's survival alone
Compare creationism and traducianism as Reformed accounts of the origin of each individual soul
Explain how sin has corrupted the whole person in all the faculties of soul and body
Analyze biblical examples showing how the condition of the body and the life of the soul affect one another
Describe the faculties of the soul as the Reformed tradition has identified them, including mind, will, and affections
Construct a written account of the human person as a unity of body and soul supported by Scripture and the Westminster Standards
Evaluate materialism, the view that a person is only a physical body, in light of Scripture's teaching on the soul
Evaluate gnostic dualism and other body-denying spiritualities against Scripture's affirmation of the body
Synthesize how Christ's incarnation, bodily resurrection, and return together accomplish the redemption of the whole person, soul and body

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (body and soul, formation from dust, goodness of the body, intermediate state versus resurrection, glorifying God in the body, dichotomy versus trichotomy, 1 Thessalonians 5:23, resurrection hope, soul's origin, whole-person theology, materialism, body-denying spiritualities, whole-person redemption). Split the grade 11 evaluation into separate objectives on materialism and on gnostic or ascetic dualism. Folded 'God cares about both body and soul' into a Gospel-based objective on Jesus' ministry. Dropped the vague 'soul lives on after death' item in favor of a fuller objective on what happens to body and soul at death. Added objectives on Christ's true body and reasonable soul, Heidelberg Q1, sin's corruption of soul and body, the interplay of body and soul, and the faculties of the soul. Dropped WLC Q93 and WCF 13.1, which address the covenant of works and sanctification, and anchored objectives to WCF 4.2, 6.2, 9.1, 32.1-3, WSC Q22, Q37, Q38, and HC Q1 and Q57. Image-of-God and sanctity-of-life content is left to sibling sub-topics.
